summary: Explains that WinRM only allows local Administrators by default; winrm configSDDL default opens an ACL editor to grant other users Read and Execute. Non-admin accounts have limited usefulness.
questions: Can a non-admin user connect to Windows over WinRM?
How do I allow a regular user to use WinRM?
What permissions does a user need to run commands over WinRM?

answer_card.title: Allowing non-administrator WinRM access
answer_card.answer_md:
By default only members of local **Administrators** can connect. Run:

```powershell
winrm configSDDL default
```

This opens an ACL editor; give the user or group at least **Read** and **Execute**. Most admin tasks still need admin rights, so non-admin accounts are of limited use.
